title: Dark pee is usually thirst.
Pink or brown never is.
What urine colour does and does not tell you

items.name: What the yellow range measures
body: The yellow comes from urobilin,
a pigment left over when the body
breaks down old red blood cells
Roughly the same amount leaves
each day, so what changes the shade
is the water it is diluted in
Drink less and the kidneys hold water
back, so the urine darkens
toward deep yellow or amber

items.name: A gauge, not a measuring cup
body: The NHS target is simple: drink enough
that your pee is a clear pale yellow
The Eatwell Guide suggests 6 to 8 cups
or glasses of fluid a day, and tea
and coffee count toward it
US reference figures look very different
- about 3.7 litres of total water for men,
2.7 for women, a fifth of it from food

items.name: Colours that mean nothing
body: The NHS names beetroot specifically:
a recent portion can turn pee pink
and it is not blood
Riboflavin passes out as an almost
fluorescent yellow and fades
once the dose does
Starting a new medicine can turn urine
red or brown - phenazopyridine,
rifampicin, senna-based laxatives

items.name: Judge by timing, not by shade
body: If the change started within a day
of a new tablet, a big beetroot salad
or a supplement, and clears when
that stops, you have your answer
If nothing on that list lines up,
stop guessing

items.name: Pink or red overrides the colour chart
body: The NHS is unusually blunt: ask for
an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111
if there is blood in your pee
Even with no other symptoms, even the
first time, even a small amount, even
if you are not sure it is blood
The reason given is equally blunt:
it can be a sign of cancer, which is
easier to treat when found early

items.name: No pain is the typical presentation
body: NIDDK notes it takes only a small
amount of blood to change the colour,
so a faint pink is not a milder finding
In most cases visible blood causes
no pain and no other symptoms at all
Being on a blood thinner is a reason
to get it looked at, not a reason
to shrug it off as expected

items.name: Brown and cloudy deserve their own note
body: Deep brown but clear can mean bilirubin
is spilling into the urine, which points
at the liver or bile ducts
It can also follow a punishing workout
or a heavy fall - muscle breakdown
releasing pigment, a same-day problem
Cloudy with burning, urgency, fever
or flank pain fits a urinary tract infection

headline: Drink toward a colour rather than a number,
and count the tea and coffee
The first pee of the morning is darker
because it has been concentrating overnight -
what matters is whether it lightens
tip: Never stop or adjust a prescribed medicine because it changed your urine colour - the prescriber can tell you in seconds whether it is expected
Wondering whether a pink tinge is worth someone's time? The NHS answer is yes, the first time, even without symptoms
